goal: Replace the leveldb-based block index store so multiple processes can safely read block data at once
Lets kernel-library consumers like external indexers read a live node's block index without waiting for shutdown
reviewability: Paused, author reworking: the author drafted this to redesign the WAL application and locking model
Reviewing the current locking code now would likely be invalidated by the planned rework
agreement: Broad concept ACK for moving off leveldb for kernel use cases (theuni, ismaelsadeeq, marcofleon, l0rinc, stickies-v, HowHsu, craigraw)
Unaddressed objection: cross-process WAL race can cause spurious failure or double-apply, no full fix yet (willcl-ark)
Nonblocking objection: flag-file deletion isn't durable on Windows, risking inconsistent state (stickies-v)
Author agrees the locking model needs more work and paused the PR to redesign it (sedited)
Earlier corruption/atomicity concerns were substantially addressed by adding WAL and checksums (ryanofsky, shahsb)

categories.name: indexes
why: P2 because it touches the core block index database that all nodes rely on for integrity
Adds checksums and WAL for better corruption resistance but also introduces new unresolved locking/race risks
Benchmarks show modest startup and disk gains with a slight reindex-time regression, so impact is not decisive yet

categories.name: kernel
why: P2 because it removes a real node dependency (leveldb) from kernel code, which is central to the kernel project's goals
Unlocks concrete external demand, such as josibake's working proof-of-concept letting Electrs index via libbitcoinkernel without waiting for shutdown
Not yet API-stable or wired into read-only kernel usage, and the author is still reworking core locking behavior
